title: Review of the dense sink-escape finding on fresh seed 95: mar-40 rods escape growing sink discs 0.61 vs 0.21 at mar 0 (22/36 vs 4/19), as claimed; the selection gradient was not re-measured
summary: Re-ran the finding's world (ARM S, disc_dt 50, 128^2, 320 frames) at mar 40 and mar 0 on fresh seed 95 and applied the author's fate.py to labkit's frames and the disc log. Escape share 22/36 = 0.61 at mar 40 against 4/19 = 0.21 at mar 0 (2.9x; the finding reports 0.53/0.56 vs 0.15/0.22). Persistent splits 21 (generation 4) at mar 40 and 12 (generation 3) at mar 0. fate.py's selection part needs extract.py's dividing-rod table, which is not in the contribution, so the D gradient and the S-vs-I distance per cycle were not checked.

observations.M: rerun/S_s95/fate.txt: of 36 bodies inside a disc's final radius one frame after it opened, 22 escape, 14 dissolve; rerun/S_mar0_s95/fate.txt: 4 of 19 escape. rerun/S_s95/sheet.png t=350-1600: rods leave the expanding dark discs.

seeds_run.result: pass for the escape advantage: 0.61 (22/36) at mar 40 vs 0.21 (4/19) at mar 0

controls_run.M: rerun/S_mar0_s95 (mar 0, same seed and disc stream)

verdicts.limitation: One fresh seed; the disc stream is the same in both arms, but fewer bodies are caught at mar 0 (19 vs 36) because the mar-0 population is smaller, so the shares rest on small counts. I did not rerun arm I, the rear-tip test (c00's mtips.py) or the selection regression (extract.py is not in the contribution).
